title: Supreme Court shields Birbhum 'Stone King' Tulu Mondal from arrest if he returns by Nov 17
dek: The stone trader, wanted in Bengal over alleged illegal quarrying and now abroad, assured the court he would come back to Kolkata from Dubai and face the cases.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Supreme Court on Wednesday protected Mohammad Nazibuddin Mondal, a Birbhum stone trader known as Tulu Mondal or the "Stone King", from arrest or other coercive action. In return, he must come back to Kolkata from Dubai by 17 November. He faces criminal cases in West Bengal over alleged illegal stone quarrying and trading.

A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu recorded his assurance that he would return and pursue his legal remedies, a news agency reported. The protection runs for three weeks from the day he arrives, according to reports by two Bengali channels. One of them said he cannot face punitive action until 7 December, and that the court left the way open for action if he does not return. Reports differ on some dates, and the written order was not yet available.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta appeared for the state, the same channel reported. He argued that the case should not be treated as a political dispute, that Mondal was allegedly linked to a wider criminal syndicate, and that he could influence the investigation once back. Mondal's lawyer said he was willing to return and cooperate.

On 22 September, the Calcutta High Court refused him protection. A report in August said that an Interpol Red Corner Notice and an arrest warrant had been issued against him.
